sb_prompt: DO YOU BELIEVE THAT THE US GOVERNMENT SHOULD PROVIDE UNIVERSAL HEALTH INSURANCE
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: You got the call?
ParticipantB: Yeah, I did. Just got off my feet.
ParticipantA: Same here. I'm an agent, so I talk to a lot of folks about stuff like this.
ParticipantB: Oh, really? I'm a nurse, so I'm hearing it everywhere too.
ParticipantA: Yeah, exactly. My cousin went bankrupt just last year because of cancer.
ParticipantB: No way. That's awful. Did he have insurance?
ParticipantA: No, he didn't. He's got the coverage now, though, through that new program he signed up for.
ParticipantB: Really? That's huge. I see so many patients who die just because they can't afford a blood test.
ParticipantA: Tell me about it. It makes my job weird sometimes. I show houses to people, but I know half of them can't even fix a pipe without going into debt.
ParticipantB: It's crazy how life-and-death stuff gets buried under rent and mortgage bills.
ParticipantA: Right? My cousin says the stress almost killed him before the diagnosis even stuck.
ParticipantB: I've had a patient last week who lost his leg because he skipped an appointment to work two jobs.
ParticipantA: Man, that breaks my heart. I tell my clients all the time, "Health is the only thing you can't resell."
ParticipantB: Exactly. If you lose your health, you lose everything. So yeah, I think the government absolutely has to step in.
ParticipantA: Me too. Though, I'll admit, I worry about the wait times. My cousin waited six months just for a specialist.
ParticipantB: That's the scary part. I worry that if we rush it, we just clog the whole system.
ParticipantA: True. But if you wait six months for a heart attack treatment, does the wait matter?
ParticipantB: No, it doesn't. The outcome is the same either way, just painful.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I guess that settles it for me. It's not about the system being perfect, it's about being alive.
ParticipantB: That's a good point. I'm on board.
ParticipantA: Cool. Thanks for talking it out with me.
ParticipantB: Yeah, you too. Good luck with the houses.
ParticipantA: Will do. Bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
